question: Does the exact production DBI/Khronon background admit rigorous finite-X bounds showing that the neutral Khronon approaches pressureless adiabatic matter rapidly enough to organize the baseline completed-U1 early-time gradient expansion?

scope.DBI_parameter: lambda_D>0; keep distinct from completion lambda_HL
scope.production_definitions: r=X/s, t=X/(s+1), rho=2mu_K^2 X(1+t), p=2mu_K^2 r t, w=p/rho, ca2=r/[s(s+X)], cs2=ca2/[1+(k/k_star)^2]

acceptance: simplify w exactly to X/[s(s+1+X)] and ca2 exactly to X/[s^2(s+X)]
using s>=ell X prove 0<=w<=1/[ell(ell+1)X] and 0<=ca2<=1/[ell^2(ell+1)X^2] for every X>0
use the exact production definition to prove 0<=cs2<=ca2
translate the bounds with X=x0/a^3 to w<=a^3/[ell(ell+1)x0] and ca2<=a^6/[ell^2(ell+1)x0^2]
verify exact asymptotic coefficients lim_{X->infinity} X w=1/[ell(ell+1)] and lim X^2 ca2=1/[ell^2(ell+1)]
verify rho/X ->2mu_K^2(ell+1)/ell, p->2mu_K^2/ell^2, so rho is dust-like a^-3 while pressure tends to a constant and w->0
verify M_K/X^(3/2)->mu_K(ell+1)sqrt(ell), hence k_star=a M_K is proportional to a^-7/2 and fixed-k cs2/ca2->1 toward the early branch
connect to the production adiabatic relation delta_khr=(3/4)(1+w)delta_gamma: its fractional deviation from the dust relation is exactly w and therefore obeys the displayed bound
do not assert that an unspecified EFT onset is numerically deep enough in this regime; retain onset evaluation as a separate physical parameter/domain check
next_if_pass: derive the baseline O(k^2) adiabatic C2 coefficient treating Khronon as a controlled dust-like component plus explicitly bounded w,ca2 corrections; evaluate the correction at the eventual frozen EFT onset rather than silently setting it to zero.
non_claims: does not select a_EFT or completion parameters
does not claim the finite-onset Khronon correction is numerically negligible before evaluation
does not derive the photon/ur anisotropic O(k^2) coefficients
does not implement completed-U1 CLASS feedback
